scenarios.title: Bounded Queue & Backpressure
scenarios.engineering_question: Does overload stay memory-bounded while accepted work reaches an explicit outcome?
scenarios.why_now: A bounded queue is required before capacity and recovery experiments scale up.
scenarios.observed_gap: The prior S2 closure did not persist every V3 bound and wait signal or independently recompute acceptance from numeric evidence; its 30-profile result is retained as historical baseline only until a fresh strict-evidence rerun passes.
proposed_design: Combine a durable queue with a bounded process-local async queue and semaphore.
Bound depth, bytes, age, and time; reject excess work with Retry-After.
Retry only transient failures with backoff, jitter, and a global budget; isolate poison work.
Scale CPU workers from queue telemetry while keeping the GPU worker count at one.
implementation_summary: The existing task create and confirmation boundaries now reserve durable PostgreSQL queue capacity atomically with idempotency and task collection state when durable mode is enabled.
Accepted idempotency replay returns the original task without another depth or byte reservation; rejected capacity does not reserve the key.
Canonical UTF-8 item size fails with 413 while aggregate depth or byte pressure fails with 429 and an integer Retry-After.
A dedicated bounded task queue worker, separate from the lifecycle worker, claims with SKIP LOCKED and owner/epoch leases, enforces local count and byte budgets, and applies retry/DLQ policy.
Durable task dispatch releases the legacy operations-ledger advisory and file lock before external Airflow HTTP, while fenced row-level PostgreSQL ownership protects the task and effect commit.
Terminal queue, effect, and task detail rows are compacted under frozen row and age limits into fixed-cardinality rollups; the JSON task collection is retained only as a bounded rollback mirror.

The operational-safety checkpoint adds bounded pre-FastAPI ingress, approval-state bounds, idempotency tombstones, deadline and effect fencing, fair runtime polling, evidence-backed outcome_unknown handling, cutover and rollback parity, exact parent-bound executor cleanup, portable process-tree RSS, and globally bounded downstream GPU work.

The first clean strict run exposed a real CPU downstream-cap bypass and a worker-restart queue-wait evidence gap. A rejected deterministic submission is now reset to reserved only after absence is proven; ambiguous effects move directly to outcome_unknown, and pre-restart queue-wait histograms are retained for final evidence.

The external E/G/H preflight confirmed queue-wait count 520 for every E repetition, CPU downstream peaks at or below 8, and 20 transient G items in DLQ. Its first G run exposed a projection-only reason-precedence bug; retry-budget and attempts-exhausted terminal reasons now take precedence over their generic last failure class.

Point-private evidence and cleanup were retained. Closed concurrency is now frozen at 64 before acceptance; no pilot result is credited.
